title: How to Get a Musty Smell Out of Your HVAC System
h1: Why Does My HVAC System Smell Musty, and How Do I Get Rid of It?
description: A musty smell from your vents usually means moisture is sitting somewhere in the system. Find out where it comes from and how to clear the odor for good.
quick_answer: A musty smell usually means moisture is collecting somewhere in the system, such as the drain pan, condensate line, evaporator coil or ductwork, and something is growing there. Replace the filter, clear the drain line, and have the coil and ducts inspected. Masking the odor won't fix it. Removing the moisture source will.
body:
When the air coming out of your vents smells like a wet towel left in a gym bag, your system is telling you something. That smell almost always comes from moisture that's sitting where it shouldn't, and from the mildew or bacteria that grow in it.

Where does a musty HVAC smell come from?

Your air conditioner pulls moisture out of the air as it cools. That water drips off the evaporator coil into a drain pan and runs out through a condensate line. When any part of that path isn't working, water sits, and the smell follows. Common sources:

  • A clogged condensate drain line. Algae and sludge build up in the line, water backs up into the pan, and it starts to smell.
  • A dirty evaporator coil. Dust sticks to the wet coil and becomes a food source for mildew.
  • A rusted or cracked drain pan that holds standing water.
  • Dirty or damp ductwork, especially duct runs in the attic or crawl space where condensation can form.
  • An old, damp filter that's been in too long.

Coastal homes in San Diego and Orange County see this more often because the outdoor air carries more moisture. Systems that sit unused through a mild spring and then kick on in summer can also smell musty for the first few cycles.

What can you check yourself?

Some of the fixes are easy. With the system turned off at the thermostat, work through these:

  1. Change the air filter. If it looks gray, damp or smells, swap it out.
  2. Look at the drain pan under the indoor unit, often in the attic, garage or a hall closet. Standing water means the line is clogged.
  3. Clear the condensate line. Many systems have a cleanout tee near the indoor unit. A wet/dry vacuum on the outdoor end of the line can pull out a clog.
  4. Check the supply registers. Pull a vent cover and look for dark spots or dust that looks damp.
  5. Look for leaks. Water stains on ceilings near the air handler point to an overflowing pan.

Avoid spraying air fresheners or scented products into the return. They cover the smell for a day and add more residue for things to grow on.

When does it take a professional cleaning?

If the smell comes back after a new filter and a clear drain line, the source is usually the coil or the ducts. Cleaning an evaporator coil means opening the air handler, which is best left to a technician. Duct cleaning and sanitizing takes specialized equipment to reach the full length of each run.

During an HVAC tune-up or repair visit, we inspect the coil, pan and drain, clean what needs it, and look for the root cause. Sometimes that's a duct with a gap pulling in damp attic air, or a system that's oversized and shuts off before it can remove enough humidity.

Is a musty smell from the AC dangerous?

A faint, short-lived odor isn't an emergency, but it shouldn't be ignored. Mildew and mold spores can irritate allergies and asthma, and they spread through the house every time the fan runs. If anyone in the home has breathing problems, deal with it sooner rather than later.

Different smells mean different things. A musty smell points to moisture. A burning or electrical smell, or a rotten egg smell, is something else. If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility from outside.

How do you keep the musty smell from coming back?

  • Replace filters on schedule, more often during heavy use or wildfire season.
  • Have the condensate line flushed during your annual maintenance.
  • Keep indoor humidity in a comfortable range. A whole-home dehumidifier can help in damp coastal homes.
  • Seal and insulate ducts in hot attics so they don't sweat.
  • Consider a UV light at the coil, which helps keep mold and bacteria from growing on wet surfaces.
faqs: Why does my AC smell musty only when it first turns on?

When the system sits idle, water left in the drain pan or on the coil can grow mildew. The first blast of air carries that odor through the house. It often fades after a few minutes, but it means the coil or drain needs cleaning.
Can I spray disinfectant into my air vents?
It isn't a good idea. Sprays can't reach the coil or most of the duct, and some leave residue that collects dust. Find and remove the moisture source, then have the coil and ducts cleaned if needed.
Does a musty smell mean there's mold in my ducts?
Not always. The most common source is the drain pan or coil, not the ducts. An inspection can tell you where the growth is, and whether duct cleaning is needed at all.
How often should the condensate drain be cleaned?
Once a year during a maintenance visit is enough for most homes. Systems that run a lot in humid weather may need it more often, and any sign of standing water means it's time now.
